 1.0     Version History
**********************************

- Version 1.3  (03/02/2011)
      Added the Clockwork Vault puzzle solution and fixed two shop prices that
      were swapped. Rewrote the final boss strategy after some very helpful
      mail.

- Version 1.2  (11/20/2010)

      Bramble Labyrinth.

- Version 1.0  (08/14/2010)
      First complete release.

 2.0     Introduction and conventions
**********************************

This is a complete walkthrough for The Ember Crown, an invented role-playing
game that exists only so this document can test a guide reader. Every town,
monster and item below is made up. Any resemblance to a real game is a sign
that role-playing games have used the same ideas for forty years.

The walkthrough follows the main story in order. Each section lists the
monsters you meet, the treasure you can find, and the shops in the area,
followed by a description of the route and strategies for anything dangerous.
General questions are answered in the FAQ at the end.

Slang:

ST:

Single-target. It hits one thing.

MT:

Multi-target. It hits everything on one side.

!Special:

Monster attacks marked with an exclamation point are physical specials, usually
stronger than a normal Attack and often carrying a status effect.

For more on the conventions used by old text guides, see
http://www.example.com/text-guides (an example address that goes nowhere).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 3.1.1   Harrowgate
**********************************

  Opponents:
  Hollowlurker (#1), Wispgolem (#2), Hollowsnapper (#3)

  Container contents:
  Swift Boots, Camp Kit, Smoke Bomb, Antivenom, 2700 Gil

Harrowgate is where the story picks up speed. You arrive with Isolde, Corvin
and Maro, and almost immediately somebody asks you to do something
unreasonable. Save before you open that door. Trust me on this one.

Preparation: Put Maro in the Back Row. Physical attacks from the back do half
damage, but Maro will be casting anyway, and you'll take half damage in return.

Monster formations:

(Outside)
Hollowlurker, Hollowlurker (10/16)
Wispgolem, Hollowlurker (6/16)

(Inside)
Hollowsnapper, Hollowsnapper, Wispgolem (11/16)
Wispgolem, Hollowsnapper (5/16)

Hollowlurker enemies are the ones to watch. They have a habit of using !Lunge
on whoever is lowest on HP, and around level 4 that can finish off a weakened
mage. Wispgolem absorbs Holy, so check your MT spells before you fire them off.
As for Hollowsnapper, it is a self-destructive little thing with a 33 % chance
to hurt itself whenever you hit it without killing it.

Item Shop:
Smelling Salts          90
Eye Balm                60
Phoenix Quill          600
Tonic                   40
Camp Kit               900
Ether Drop            1200
 Stock up on Tonics. Nothing else here is urgent, and you'll want the money for
the weapon shop.

Weapon Shop:
Storm Spear           1850
Hunting Bow           1150
Moonsilver Blade      1400
Quartz Rod            1250
 Buy the Quartz Rod for Isolde if you can afford it. It's a large upgrade.

Innkeeper: Rooms are 20 Gil. Breakfast is extra, and it's mostly porridge.
Isolde: We'll take two.

Hidden Items: There's a Antivenom in the barrel behind the well, and a Lucky
Coin in the clock of the mayor's house. Leave the chest in the cellar alone for
now; its contents change into something much better later in the game, and
you'll come back this way anyway.

When you're ready, head west out of Harrowgate. The _Ember_Crown_ itself is
mentioned for the first time here, in a conversation that is easy to miss. It's
worth reading *all* of it.

 3.1.2   Traveling to the Old Quarry
**********************************

  Opponents:
  Wispbeak (#4), Rustmoth (#5), Gravegolem (#6)

  Container contents:
  Ether Drop, Smoke Bomb, Owl Pendant, Stillwater Bead, 2600 Gil

Traveling to the Old Quarry is where the story picks up speed. You arrive with
Maro, Pell and Tamsin, and almost immediately somebody asks you to do something
unreasonable. Somebody on the message boards swears there's a secret here.
There isn't.

Preparation: Put Tamsin in the Back Row. Physical attacks from the back do half
damage, but Tamsin will be casting anyway, and you'll take half damage in
return.

Monster formations:

(Outside)
Wispbeak, Wispbeak (10/16)
Rustmoth, Wispbeak (6/16)

(Inside)
Gravegolem, Gravegolem, Rustmoth (11/16)
Rustmoth, Gravegolem (5/16)

Wispbeak enemies are the ones to watch. They have a habit of using !Lunge on
whoever is lowest on HP, and around level 5 that can finish off a weakened
mage. Rustmoth absorbs Water, so check your MT spells before you fire them off.
As for Gravegolem, it is a self-destructive little thing with a 33 % chance to
hurt itself whenever you hit it without killing it.

At the crossroads you'll get two options:
         Take the cliff path.
         Take the river path.
The cliff path is shorter but has twice as many encounters. The river path has
a hidden chest behind the waterfall with a Ward Charm, which is worth the
detour.

Hidden Items: There's a Camp Kit in the barrel behind the well, and a
Stillwater Bead in the clock of the mayor's house. Leave the chest in the
cellar alone for now; its contents change into something much better later in

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 3.2.4   The battle with the Gloomlurker Queen
**********************************

Gloomlurker Queen waits at the bottom of the stairs, and the game is not subtle
about it: the floor is covered in the bones of adventurers who did not read
this section first.

Gloomlurker Queen
Level: 14, HP: 17010, MP: 168
Steal: Hi-Tonic (rare), Hi-Tonic (common), Win: Smelling Salts (always)
Weakness: Fire
Special: !Spit: sets Confuse, Attack x 1.5
Vulnerable to: Blind, Silence, Stop
Attacks: Attack, Chill Touch, Tidal Rush

Open with Isolde casting a Fire spell; it does nearly double damage. Keep Wren
on healing duty, because the second phase starts with an MT attack that will
flatten anyone below about 300 HP. When Gloomlurker Queen says "You cannot burn
what is already ash!", it is about to switch to its counter-attack pattern, so
stop using physical attacks for one turn.

Note: if you are beyond the shame of any adventurer, you can steal a rare item
here with enough patience. It costs about twenty minutes and most of your
dignity.

 3.4.4   The battle with the Hollowdrake Queen
**********************************

Hollowdrake Queen waits at the bottom of the stairs, and the game is not subtle
about it: the floor is covered in the bones of adventurers who did not read
this section first.

Hollowdrake Queen
Level: 20, HP: 81900, MP: 640
Steal: Antivenom (rare), Hi-Tonic (common), Win: Eye Balm (always)
Weakness: Ice
Special: !Spit: sets Stop, Attack x 1.5
Vulnerable to: Doom, Petrify, Slow
Attacks: Attack, Tidal Rush, Rockfall

Open with Tamsin casting a Ice spell; it does nearly double damage. Keep Wren
on healing duty, because the second phase starts with an MT attack that will
flatten anyone below about 480 HP. When Hollowdrake Queen says "You cannot burn
what is already ash!", it is about to switch to its counter-attack pattern, so
stop using physical attacks for one turn.

here with enough patience. It costs about twenty minutes and most of your
dignity.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 3.7.4   The Clockwork Vault puzzle, explained slowly and with considerable patience for everyone involved
**********************************

The vault has four dials, and each one rotates the two next to it. The game
never explains this. Set them in this order:

Dial         Turns   Facing
North        2       Sun
East         1       Moon
South        3       Star
West         0       Sun

If you get it wrong, a Rustgolem drops from the ceiling. It is not hard, just
embarrassing.

If you skipped the side room earlier, now is a good time to regret it.

Preparation: Put Corvin in the Back Row. Physical attacks from the back do half
damage, but Corvin will be casting anyway, and you'll take half damage in
return.

Monster formations:

(Outside)
Cindermaw, Cindermaw (10/16)
Gloomdrake, Cindermaw (6/16)

(Inside)
Cinderwight, Cinderwight, Gloomdrake (11/16)
Gloomdrake, Cinderwight (5/16)

Cindermaw enemies are the ones to watch. They have a habit of using !Lunge on
whoever is lowest on HP, and around level 28 that can finish off a weakened
mage. Gloomdrake absorbs Ice, so check your MT spells before you fire them off.
As for Cinderwight, it is a self-destructive little thing with a 33 % chance to
hurt itself whenever you hit it without killing it.

Item Shop:
Warp Shard             700
Antivenom               45
Smoke Bomb             150
Smelling Salts          90
Camp Kit               900
Hi-Tonic               250
 Stock up on Tonics. Nothing else here is urgent, and you'll want the money for
the weapon shop.

Weapon Shop:
Duskfang              4050
Thorn Whip           15300
Hunting Bow           9900
Steel Glaive          3150
 Buy the Steel Glaive for Pell if you can afford it. It's a large upgrade.

Innkeeper: Rooms are 180 Gil. Breakfast is extra, and it's mostly porridge.
Pell: We'll take two.

Hidden Items: There's a Tonic in the barrel behind the well, and a Iron Will
Ring in the clock of the mayor's house. Leave the chest in the cellar alone for
now; its contents change into something much better later in the game, and
you'll come back this way anyway.

When you're ready, head north out of Greywold. The _Ember_Crown_ itself is
mentioned for the first time here, in a conversation that is easy to miss. It's
worth reading *all* of it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 3.10.4  The battle with the Rustsnapper Queen
**********************************

Rustsnapper Queen waits at the bottom of the stairs, and the game is not subtle
about it: the floor is covered in the bones of adventurers who did not read
this section first.

Rustsnapper Queen
Level: 38, HP: 148770, MP: 1520
Steal: Smoke Bomb (rare), Smoke Bomb (common), Win: Phoenix Quill (always)
Weakness: Wind
Special: !Crush: sets Sleep, Attack x 1.5
Vulnerable to: Silence, Slow, Doom, Poison
Attacks: Attack, Rockfall, Chill Touch

Open with Pell casting a Wind spell; it does nearly double damage. Keep Tamsin
on healing duty, because the second phase starts with an MT attack that will
flatten anyone below about 1020 HP. When Rustsnapper Queen says "You cannot
burn what is already ash!", it is about to switch to its counter-attack
pattern, so stop using physical attacks for one turn.

Note: if you are beyond the shame of any adventurer, you can steal a rare item
here with enough patience. It costs about twenty minutes and most of your
dignity.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 6.0     Frequently Asked Questions
**********************************

Q: Can I go back to Harrowgate after the bridge collapses?
A: Yes, once you have the airship. The bridge itself is gone for good.

Q: Is the Crown Edge worth the trouble?
A: It's the strongest sword in the game, so yes, but only if you enjoy fighting
the same monster forty times in a row for a rare drop.

Q: Why does my save file say 'Chapter 0'?
A: That's a known bug if you save during the opening cutscene. It's harmless.
